headline: SKYWARD goes online — four pilots, one seeded sky
lede: Slot a shipped room codes for the flight school: up to four pilots share the same island, weather cell and strip over the arcade's relay, 180 seconds on the bell, score wins. Open seats fly the same autopilot the checks graduate on, a silent pilot never stalls the sky, and the folded hash proves every box flew the same world.

notes.text: Every box simulates every seat — humans on the wire, open seats on the planner — so a pilot's hull is real physics in every sky, not a streamed ghost; the analog stick rides the wire at 1/100 (a stick game stays a stick game).

Two takeover laws for vanished pilots (relay-ordered roster, tick-anchored silence for handshake-then-die sockets) plus a new lockstep primitive, dropPeer — the shared plumbing got stronger for every future multiplayer game, and netcheck/roomcheck say so.
Proof: skywardcheck 233/233 with 28 new virtual-room pins, and skywardroom — two real Chromes racing over the deployed relay with a convergence check after a forced dropout.
The warden's #3407 target stayed with slot b (live hold, PR #3424) — this session rode the never-dry ladder instead and took the shelf's weakest gap, honestly scored.
